subject: Information Theory
title: What Is Noise
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is Noise.

hook.text: Static on an old radio. Snow on an analog TV. Hiss on a phone call. That's noise: the enemy of every signal.

buildup.text: Noise is any unwanted disturbance added to a signal during transmission, storage, or processing.

discovery.text: Thermal noise comes from random electron motion. It exists in every conductor above absolute zero.

twist.text: You can never eliminate noise completely. The laws of thermodynamics guarantee a minimum noise floor.

climax.text: Engineering doesn't fight noise head-on. It designs systems that work correctly despite the noise.

punchline.text: Noise is physics. Engineering is the workaround.

quiz.question: Why can't noise be completely eliminated?
options: Thermal noise is guaranteed by thermodynamics
